thread:
Priya: quick FYI  onboarding run for model 'akai-embed' (3.5B) finished. noticed a concentrated recall drop for short Japanese queries after int8-per-channel quantization.
Priya: top-line (ja-short holdout, n=6k):
Priya:  - baseline fp16 r@1: 0.912
Priya:  - akai fp16 r@1: 0.908
Priya:  - akai int8-per-channel r@1: 0.862  <-- focused on JA kana/kanji-mix queries
Priya:  - r@10 delta: -1.3%
Priya:  - mean norm shift (fp16 -> int8): -6% on JA subset
Priya: artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/akai/3771234567/ (metrics-bot uploaded)
Akiko: interesting. were JA queries tokenized into many small subwords vs baseline? which tokenizer/version used?
Priya: tokenizer: shared-bpe-v5 (same as baseline). exported with converter-v5; calibration set = default-mix-20k. seed=314
Dan: can you paste the eval command + batch distribution? microbatching sometimes exposes ordering ties on short tokens.
Priya: ran:
Priya: ```
python eval_embeds.py --model akai-embed --quant int8_per_channel --holdout ja-short --seed 314 --normalize l2 --batch-dist zipf:1-64 --knn exact
```
Chiara: two hypotheses: (1) tokenization produces many high-frequency subword tokens in JA that concentrate information in a small set of coordinates, (2) per-channel scale learned on majority-English calibration underfits those coords and clips them harder.
Akiko: i can provide a small JA-focused calibration slice (5k queries with kanji-heavy examples) to try. also can share a few failing query texts for easier reproduction.
Priya: thanks  adding that to ablation. norm stats: fp16 mean 1.02 +/-0.03 (ja subset), int8 mean 0.96 +/-0.04. coordinate-sparsity metric shows top-6 dims get +18% relative weight post-quant.
Marco: +1 on per-lang calibration. also try per-tensor quant as a quick check to see if brittleness is per-channel-specific.
Priya: queued ablations: (A) per-tensor int8, (B) per-channel with JA-targeted calibration (5k kanji-heavy), (C) post-quant L2 mean-rescale per-language. jobs: 3771234570, 3771234571, 3771234572.
metrics-bot: artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-evals/akai/3771234567/ (eval.json, nn_diffs_ja_sample.csv, coord_var.tsv)
Dan: paste a few NN diffs (sample) please, would help see whether swaps are semantically plausible or random.
Priya: sample nearest neighbor diffs:
Priya: "q42,fp16_nn1=doc_901,int8_nn1=doc_1120  # fp16: '京都の秋', int8: '大阪の観光'"
Priya: "q47,fp16_nn1=doc_77,int8_nn1=doc_77  # stable"
Priya: "q51,fp16_nn1=doc_300,int8_nn1=doc_310  # subtle swap, related docs"
Akiko: those look like rank permutations rather than catastrophic semantic mismatch  consistent with numeric jitter.
Chiara: also check token-length distribution: if JA queries become much shorter in token count, quantization noise has larger relative effect. dump token lengths for failing queries.
Priya: token-lengths for failing queries median=3 tokens (very short). added token-length.tsv to artifacts.
Marco: plan:
Marco:  - Priya: run the three ablations and produce recall@k curves k=1..50 plus failing-query snapshots (owner: Priya)
Marco:  - Akiko: provide the 5k-kanji calibration slice and a small set of human-labeled golden neighbors for 50 failing queries (owner: Akiko)
Marco:  - Chiara: review converter-v5 calibration to see if it weights calibration samples by token-length or language (owner: Chiara)
Priya: started jobs. ETA ~70m. will attach results to S3 path.
metrics-bot: rerun started (job id 3771234570)
Priya: quick update  per-tensor int8 reduced r@1 gap from -4.6% -> -1.2% (partial recovery). per-channel with JA-targeted calibration improved r@1 to 0.900 (nearly parity). post-quant mean-rescale also helped to 0.902.
Akiko: good sign. targeted calibration and simple rescale both working indicates calibrator sample mismatch was main driver.
Dan: can you check neighbor margin (delta similarity between nn1 and nn2) distribution for recovered vs failed queries? small margins are vulnerable to swapping.
Priya: margin stats: recovered queries median margin 0.07, failed queries median margin 0.012. adding margin_hist.tsv to artifacts.
Chiara: given this, recommend: (1) add a JA-aware calibration option in converter, (2) run a short-token-length check during onboard smoke and warn if >x% of holdout are length<=3, (3) consider a fallback to per-tensor quant for models that show strong token-length sensitivity.
Marco: agree. add tickets ENGML-9801 (converter per-lang calib), ENGML-9802 (embed-smoke token-length check), ENGML-9803 (quant-fallback policy).
Priya: created tickets and uploaded a tiny notebook that reproduces the rescale ablation and a README for SREs. artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/akai/3771234572/
metrics-bot: final artifacts uploaded and job closed.
Akiko: thanks everyone. i'll curate the 50 golden neighbor examples and attach to ENGML-9801 so we can add them to calibrator test set.
Marco: nice triage. once tickets are green we should add a short paragraph to the embed runbook on token-length sensitivity for small multilingual models.
Priya: will draft runbook note in the ticket. closing loop for now :thumbsup:
